claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions. Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child I'm asking about. His name is Alex and he's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Alex is 8 years old, which is under 16, so that's a good start.

Now I need to ask you a few more questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to understand your relationship with Alex:

**Do you live with Alex, or if you don't live with him, are you paying at least the same amount as Child Benefit (or the equivalent in kind) towards looking after him - for example on food, clothes or pocket money?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me, but I do contribute towards his upkeep. I help out with things like clothes and other bits he needs - I give about £26 a week for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand the living arrangement better:

**Who does Alex live with, and for how long has he been living with them?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his mum, my ex-partner. He's been living with her for quite a while now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. I have a few more important questions:

**Is Alex's mum currently claiming Child Benefit for him?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, she's not claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to confirm a few final details:

**Are you contributing the £26 per week regularly (weekly, monthly, or in regular amounts), and has this been ongoing? Also, is Alex in full-time education?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I contribute the £26 every week regularly. And yes, Alex is in school - he's only 8, so he's in primary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! Based on the information you've provided, you appear to be ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

- **Alex meets the age requirement** - He's 8 years old, which is under 16
- **You're considered responsible for him** - Even though Alex doesn't live with you, you're contributing £26 per week regularly towards his upkeep (clothes and necessities), which meets the threshold for being responsible for a child
- **You live in the UK** - You meet the residency requirement
- **No one else is claiming** - Alex's mother is not currently claiming Child Benefit for him, and only one person can claim per child

**What you need to know:**

- You'll need to make a claim for Child Benefit for Alex
- Please note: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may have to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge
- If Alex's mother decides she wants to claim Child Benefit in the future, you would need to agree between yourselves who will claim, as only one person can receive it for the same child

Would you like to know more about how to make a claim or have any other questions?
